setup: Set up a flat bench inside a power rack with safety pins adjusted just below your target hold height.
Lie supine on the bench with your eyes directly under the bar, feet flat on the floor, and shoulder blades retracted and depressed.
Grip the barbell with a full, pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack the bar with straight arms over your chest.
steps: Lower the bar with control to your predetermined target position, typically just off the chest or at your specific sticking point.
Bring the bar to a dead stop and maintain maximal tension, resisting any movement for the prescribed duration.
Press the bar forcefully back to full lockout once the hold time is completed, then carefully rack the barbell.
instructions.breathing: Take a deep diaphragmatic breath and brace your core prior to descending, maintaining pressurized, shallow breaths during the hold without losing upper-back tension.
cues: Crush the bar with your hands.
Pull shoulder blades back and down into the bench.
Drive your feet into the floor.
Freeze the bar in place without letting it drift.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the barbell to slowly drift or bounce during the hold.
common_faults.correction: Lock into position and keep full-body tension constant throughout the entire target duration.

common_faults.fault: Losing scapular retraction, causing the shoulders to roll forward.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper back pinned tightly into the bench and your chest high.

common_faults.fault: Performing the hold without safety pins set at the correct height.
common_faults.correction: Position rack safety pins immediately below the hold position to catch the barbell safely in the event of fatigue.

precautions: Always perform this movement inside a power rack with properly adjusted safety pins or with an attentive spotter, as sudden muscle failure is common during isometric holds.
Do not bounce the bar off the safety pins or drop it onto your chest.

name: Barbell Bench Press Isometric Hold
summary: A static upper-body exercise where a loaded barbell is held motionless at a specific point in the bench press range of motion to build sticking-point strength and joint stability.
